nodes.label: hiQ v. LinkedIn case law
nodes.rationale: hiQ won on CFAA and lost on state law — $500k judgment under CA trespass to chattels; avoiding CFAA does not immunise against contract/tort claims.

nodes.label: JA4 TLS fingerprint standard
nodes.rationale: JA3 is dead since Chrome 110 randomised extension order (Jan 2023); JA4 is universally adopted by Cloudflare, AWS WAF, Akamai, VirusTotal as of 2026.

nodes.label: Fingerprint coherence principle
nodes.rationale: Detection needs only one layer inconsistent with the others — TLS, CDP and JS fingerprint must agree on one coherent identity, not three tools configured independently.

nodes.label: Lightpanda (Zig browser)
nodes.rationale: 11x faster, 9x less memory than Chrome by skipping CSS layout, GPU compositing and font rendering; cannot handle canvas or real visual layout.

nodes.label: PyMuPDF AGPL licensing landmine
nodes.rationale: 10-50x faster than pypdfium2 but AGPL — requires open-sourcing or a commercial Artifex licence; pypdfium2 (Apache/BSD) is correct default for a permissive project.

nodes.label: Bloom filter URL dedup
nodes.rationale: 1 billion URLs at 0.1% false-positive costs ~1.8GB vs ~40GB for a plain Redis SET — a 22x saving.

nodes.label: Stripe webhook model (reference)
nodes.rationale: Up to 3 days exponential backoff, HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp.body, constant-time comparison, 5-min tolerance, dual-active secrets during rotation, dead-letter with manual replay.

nodes.label: Firecrawl PR #3396 (unmerged) Qdrant crawl dedup
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 content hash skip + deterministic UUID v5 point IDs from URL so re-crawls update in-place rather than duplicating vectors.

nodes.label: Three-runtime shape rationale
nodes.rationale: TypeScript owns orchestration (Playwright/job/HTTP), Python owns extraction (trafilatura/Docling/embeddings), Rust owns fetch (TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint control on the hot path).

nodes.label: Fetch ladder (4 tiers)
nodes.rationale: Cheapest first: tier0 plain HTTP ~5ms, tier1 TLS-impersonating ~50ms, tier2 Lightpanda ~25ms, tier3 Chromium ~2-5s. Escalate only on evidence, never a framework guess.

nodes.label: Escalation policy (content-presence test)
nodes.rationale: Content-presence in raw HTML triggers escalation, not framework name — Next.js/Nuxt often server-render real content, so escalating on framework alone burns the expensive tier for nothing.

nodes.label: Capture-and-replay profile generation
nodes.rationale: A capture harness records a real browser's handshake/JS surface and emits a profile, keeping profiles honest as browsers ship new versions.
